utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone breaks the vow, the promise so given, the besa --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Nobody from the Albanians will break the besa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- they can be strictly sanctioned by their own people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Albanians will never break a promise. A promise is always a promise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in your experience, the besa, the promise, must never be broken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Well, how can you break a promise? This is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will now ask you, Mrs. Jusufi, some questions related to the events you testified about when my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, examined you.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I can't go on anymore. I think this was enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from your testimony today, is it correct, Mrs. Jusufi, that you have made statements twice to the Prosecutor of the ICTY? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. My husband knows these things. Personally, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that your first statement to the investigator of the Prosecutor's office of the ICTY was made on the 3rd of October, 2004, you will be reminded of that and you can then confirm this to me; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I really don't understand this. Men knows these things. I really don't understand these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now that the witness is shown the document 65 ter 1D1, ID 0004. That is the page number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until we receive the image, I would like to ask Mrs. Jusufi: Is it correct that you are illiterate?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know how to write or read.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you can write your own name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, only my name, nothing else. Even my own name, I don't know how to write it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that when you were interviewed earlier by the Prosecutor, that your husband would always be with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. My husband also signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now if that is possible to show the witness 65 ter, document 1D1, 004. Can you give us the English version of the document I've mentioned? That is 1D1, 0001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see in front of you the image where you have signed?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we will ask the usher to show the witness the first page of the aforementioned document, because the witness can't see the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this signature is your personal signature?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I can't see it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mrs. Jusufi, that when you made this statement and you signed this paper, your husband was together with you?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, but he cannot move. He is an invalid. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that you never made a statement to the Prosecutor outside the presence of your husband? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: My husband is an invalid. This statement is mine, but the other one that I'm looking, that one I don't know whose it is. Maybe it's my husband's.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have answered my previous question in saying that when the investigator of the ICTY in Ljuboten interviewed you about the event, your husband was together with you in his wheelchair; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes, we both gave statements and signed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If in some of your statements it is not noted that your husband was present during the interview, that must have been a mistake of the persons who were writing that statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, he was writing. Nobody made any mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. When you made the statement -- when you made the statement, there was an interpreter for the Albanian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask that the witness is instructed not to speak simultaneously with the counsel. We have difficulties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I guess I was, but I have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you remember that you had made the statement on the same date when a statement was given by your husband, and that you were together all the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: All the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Jusufi, I know that for you, as a mother, it is very difficult to recall the events that you testify about, but I would like to ask you to still answer some questions that the learned Prosecutor asked you about at the beginning of today's trial. Is it correct that you have before, as today during your testimony, have often answered that you can't remember everything and that what your husband has stated is correct; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Ask my husband. Personally, I don't know. When he comes here to testify, you can ask him. I did what I was supposed to do here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, besides the statement that you made in October of 2004, you have recently, in Ljuboten, on the 22nd of April of this year, also made a statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. There was nothing more to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask that the witness is shown the English text, 1D4, 0016, 65 ter number 1D4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you, Mrs. Jusufi, can't read and write, can you please confirm that on the bottom, you have also signed this statement? Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here it reads that on the 22nd of April, 2007, you have had an interview with the Prosecutor, Joanne Motoike, and that as you have indicated, you have signed this statement. Do you remember now that you have made that statement?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it correct that your husband was also present when you were making this statement?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, he was. Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if by chance someone forgot to write that he was present as well during your interview, that is not your mistake; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No. My husband is an invalid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know, and I do not wish to say anything bad about you or your husband. I just wanted to know, when you have signed this statement last month, you have stated that your husband was present while you were making your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe he was. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, could I indicate that when you asked the witness to identify her statement in respect of the second statement made this year, the document on the screen was still the first statement made in 2004. On the screen now is the 2007 statement. I think we'd better check that the witness accepts this to be also a statement of hers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your warning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, The Honours have already -- have just told us that to have another look at the signature on the paper in front of you. Can you see the text document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the bottom. Is that your signature at the bottom of this document or this page?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Jusufi, at the question of the learned colleague, you have said that at 7.30 in the morning, you have taken your husband into the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mrs. Jusufi, where did you leave your husband in his wheelchair?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: In the room, of course, inside, not outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand this well, you have taken your husband into the living room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: In a room. I took him to the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was in that room at that time -- was your relative Muzafer Jusufi in the room at that time and yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He was. He came to have a coffee with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first statement that I have shown you and has the number 65 ter 1D1, on page 0003, and in the Macedonian version that is page 0007, you have said: "I put Elmaz into the other room below the staircase because I thought that it is safer there." Did you say that in that way?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor interviewed you on the 22nd of April, 2007, that is number 65 ter 1D4, 0018, you have said in point 5: "I was in a panic and I took my husband inside the house, into the living room on the left-hand side from the entrance to the house." Did you say that to the Prosecutor during the last month?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. I think in the right side, on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me, Mrs. Jusufi, that these statements about the fact where you have taken your husband when you took him into the house, significantly differ from what you have said in the first -- in the second statement and today before the Court.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I remember I took him to the room on the right side. I believe they have made a mistake when recording it or writing down my words.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today, my learned colleague have asked you when you saw the police officers, and then you testified that at 5.00 in the morning you have only heard the voices in front of your house, coming from the direction of the Orthodox Church, but that you have seen no one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in the first statement that has been showed you, and you recognised your signature, that is number 65 ter 1D1, 0002, the Macedonian version bearing the number 1D, 007, you have said that at 5.00 in the morning you had seen police in front of your house and that you have also seen them at 7.30, when you were helping your husband to come to the gate to your yard. In your statement of April 22nd, 2007, that is, number 65 ter 1D4, 0017, you have stated that you have only seen the police officers at 5.00 in the morning and that at 7.30 you have only heard them, but you have not seen them. Today, you said that you have never seen them. Is it correct, Mrs. Jusufi, that this statement of yours significantly differ whether and when you have seen the policemen?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, it's not different. It is true, as I said, as I have seen them. I saw -- I heard them, with my own ears, talking among themselves. I didn't see them when they were in the street, but I heard them talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have clarified that today, at the question of the learned colleague, because you said that you could not see through the door and the wall, through the gate and the wall. I would like to remind you that in your -- in the first statement, ID 1002, and the Macedonian version ID 0007, you have said: "Not only that I have seen the policemen, but we have also --" you have also seen a car and trucks in the street. That is written in paragraph 8?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I didn't see them outside, but there were policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the statement of April 22nd, 65 ter number 1D4, 0017, in paragraph 2, last sentence, you have said: "I've heard tanks and trucks, but I have not seen them." I ask you, Mrs. Jusufi, is it correct if I say that your statements about these facts are also significantly different?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, it is not different. It is exactly as I said. I heard them talking. I didn't say that I saw them in the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, today you have, on the question of the learned colleague, mentioned that Muzafer Jusufi was also in your house, a son of the uncle of your husband?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Muzafer is our uncle's son.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mrs. Jusufi, was anyone else in the house at that moment?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No. I didn't understand it very well. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was some of the relatives in the house, apart from Muzafer Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: There wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I say to you, Mrs. Jusufi, that on April 22 of this year, when giving the statement to the Prosecutor in Ljuboten, that is, 65 ter 1D4, 0018, paragraph 7, you have stated that in the house then there were also Imret and Muzafer Jusufi, and they were in the room to the left side, on the other side of the entry door --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: It's wrong. It's a mistake. Only Muzafer was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want to say, Mrs. Jusufi, that the investigators have made a mistake writing that Imret Jusufi was also in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: It has been recorded wrong. No, no -- or I may have misspoken. He wasn't there. Muzafer was there. Maybe I misspoke, instead of saying "Muzafer," I said "Imret," but there wasn't anyone else apart from Muzafer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the question of the learned colleague, you have said that you have taken your husband into the house to make breakfast, but that you haven't had breakfast?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, we couldn't have breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But if I say to you that in your first statement, 65 ter number 1D1, ID 0003, and Macedonian version 0007, paragraph 9, you have said that you have taken your husband inside and that you have had breakfast, then those two statements are different; is it true?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, I said I took him inside in order for me to prepare breakfast, but I never said that we did have breakfast. We couldn't have any breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if that was also written in the statement, then that is a mistake of those who were writing that statement; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: They have written it wrong. It must be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the question of the learned colleague, you have said that you have not prepared breakfast because the electricity ran out. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in the statement of April 22, 2007, number ID4, 0018 -- yes, 0018, you have said that you did not have breakfast because you have heard -- that you heard voices of policemen, and then in panic you have taken your husband into the house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And those two statements are different; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: They are not different at all, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, I will now, unfortunately, have to ask you a few questions regarding the death of your son. Before that, please tell me, do you know Fatmir Kamberi, the son of Reshat?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, he's a co-villager and a neighbour of ours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your son was in good relations with him, and there would be no reason for him to say something that would not be true; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He was a neighbour. What do you mean? I don't understand what you are asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were Rami and Fatmir good neighbours and good friends?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: They were neighbours. I don't know more than that. Just a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the question of the learned colleague, you have said that on Sunday, you have awakened at 5.00; is that correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, because every Sunday, we wake up early to say the prayers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that moment, you have gone out into the yard alone, as you have testified in your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There wasn't anyone else in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, at what time did your husband wake up, and when was it when you assisted him to get out into the yard?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: When he woke up, I assisted him. I took him out in the yard. I don't know what time exactly it was. Maybe 5.00, 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, could you remember whether that was at the same time when you also got out or was it later?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I took my husband and we went together outside because he was tired of sitting all night and of staying inside the room. I wanted him to get some fresh air.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, did you sleep at all that night?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: We didn't sleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone come into your house during the night?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, nobody came.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that your son slept in his room during the entire night?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He slept in his own room, it is correct. I'm not lying here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you woke up at 5.00, was your son still sleeping and there was no one into your -- into your yard; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He was sleeping and there wasn't anyone in our yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to go to a closed session for a while because I would like to give -- to point out a statement of one of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, I did not understand so very well everything that you have answered to the learned colleague about when and how --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... wasn't there. Don't ask me any more, please. I cannot answer your questions. I gave all the answers I had to give.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are doing very well, Mrs. Jashari [sic], thank you very much. There will not be many more, so carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel tired, Your Honour, I feel very tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think in that case, then, we'll have a little break now. And, again, that break must be for half an hour and we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to go home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... at five minutes to 6.00. We will finish your evidence in a little after the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to go home, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That won't be possible right now, but we will not be long with you after the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've said everything I wanted to say. There is nothing else left.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Just a brief issue has actually been brought to our attention. If perhaps the Court could advise Mrs. Jusufi not to answer the questions given to her by Ms. Residovic until the translation is completely finished. That way, our kind interpreters could translate everything that's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I fully appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The problem is that I think the technology in this room is something that the witness is not very well equipped to deal with. To give her extra things to think about may be counter-productive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I appreciate the problem. We hope to be very short in completing your evidence, so I hope you can bear with us while that is done. Would you please try just to listen to the question fully, until it is finished. It often helps if you can do that. And then we'll be able to continue. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, I hope that you managed to get some rest. When the learned colleague Prosecutor asked you, on the page 26, line 19 and 20, you said that your son, Rami, was asleep, and then on the page 27, you also said that when you went in to make the breakfast, that he was still asleep. And on the same page, in line 14 to 18, you said that he had woken up when the door was opened. Do you remember that, that you had stated so today?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: It is the way I described it. He was asleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mrs. Jusufi, who had woken your son up or what has woken him up?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: When the blast was heard at the front gate, he woke up. It was 7.30, about 7.30 in the morning. He did not wake up earlier than that. The blast was very powerful. The door was broken down, and he woke up. He went to the entrance door, and they killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mrs. Jusufi, at the moment when your son woke up, what were the clothes that your son had on?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: You know that when people go to sleep, they wear pyjamas. He was in his pyjamas when he went to the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, when he was hit, can you tell us, what was your son wearing? Have you seen him?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He was wearing a T-shirt and jeans.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were, Mrs. Jusufi, to tell you that in your first statement, where you've recognised your signature, 65 ter number 1D1, page 0003, Macedonian version 0008, in relation to your son, paragraph 11, you stated: "I woke him up because of the blast at the front gate. He was wearing pyjamas --"

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, I woke him up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "-- he got up and went to close the door."

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No. Maybe it's not recorded correctly. He went to close the entrance door. He was wearing pyjamas while he was asleep. He put on his clothes very quickly, and he went to close the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding this very fact, Mrs. Jusufi, in your next statement, 65 ter number 1D4, 0018, paragraph 7, you have stated: "My son was not wearing his pyjamas, but he changed his attire, and then he left the room. When my son was changing clothes, I was standing in the living room."

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's not correct. While he was asleep, he was in his pyjamas. When I woke him up, he dressed up and he went to the entrance door to close it, and they were already in the yard and they killed him. This is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later, you stated: "After my son put his clothes on, my husband and I joined two of our neighbours in the room on the left side from the front door to the house, immediately across from the front door." Regarding that same event, in your first statement, 65 ter number 1D1, ID 0003, Macedonian version 0008, in the paragraph 12 you stated: "My son went out to close the door." And then in the paragraph 13, you indicated: "At that moment -- at that moment, I was standing close to my husband. We were both of us in the corridor --"

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: It's a mistake, it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the paragraph 14, you stated: "My son was running from the bedroom to the door. He was standing with his full body exposed to the front door."

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no, it's a mistake. What I've already stated earlier, that's correct. Everything that you're reading now is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Jusufi, with regards to the persons present and with regards to the way in which your son woke up --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: There was nobody there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- and with regards to the clothes that he was wearing, everything has been entered correctly into your previous statements -- recorded incorrectly; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No. What I've stated in my statement is correct, and what you are reading now is a mistake. I don't know who is responsible for that mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also, Mrs. Jusufi, in your previous statement about this event, paragraph 14 and paragraph 15, that is, 65 ter number 1D4, ID 0018, and after that ID 0019, you have described the event of the killing of your son and you have stated: "At that moment, I've heard rifles. My son was stricken down. He was still holding the door, and the door was almost closed when he fell down."

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the statement of the 22nd of April, 1D4, ID 0018, in the paragraph 8 you stated: "The front door to the house was open. We heard shooting. My husband was at that moment near the door, in his wheelchair. I was standing beside him. My son jumped up from the sofa --"

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "-- passed my husband by and myself --"

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He passed him by and went to the entrance door, yes, yes, that's correct, to close the door, because the door was wide open. And as soon as he got to the entrance door, they killed him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic said before, "... with the intention to close the entrance door."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mrs. Jusufi, these statements contradict what you have testified today under oath, stating that you were in the room?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Everything I've stated is correct, but you have recorded things erroneously. We went to the room with my husband. Where else were we supposed to go? We couldn't stay in the yard. What you have noted down is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, to the question of the learned colleague, you have stated that as soon as your -- your son was hit, you fainted. Have you stated this today?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, when my son fell down, I lost consciousness. Then I was completely lost. We took him inside the room. I was completely lost after that. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: You're mixing things up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statement, Mrs. Jusufi, 1D1, 004 --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no, you're mixing things up here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- Macedonian version 0008, paragraph 22, you have stated: "When the men disappeared from the door, we looked at our son. He was bleeding from the two bullet wounds on his back." So your statement today, that you have fainted, does not correspond to what you have stated before; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: It's not different. As soon as I saw my son in that state, I was completely lost. You would do the same if you saw your own son.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mrs. Jusufi, who and when has moved your son from the corridor --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- the corridor next to the entrance into the room?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: When the police left, I regained consciousness, and with Muzafer then, we put him inside the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the bleeding from the wounds, from the bullet wounds, was strong, you would agree with this?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Of course he was bleeding heavily.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All his clothes were blood-stained; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. We tried to -- we took the sheet and we tried to tie his wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: His T-shirt and his trousers were completely blood-stained; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When your son -- when he woke up, were his trousers on, as you have stated today, he buttoned up his trousers, and nobody pulled the trousers off him; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: We didn't take off his trousers. We didn't at all. What do you mean, take off his trousers?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of our learned colleague, you have stated that inside the house you remained for another 12 hours; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I didn't go out at all. Where was I supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And nobody came during that time into your house; is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, how soon did your son die?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know to this day, because even when you mention it now, I feel very weak. I don't know how long; 15 minutes, 20 minutes. I wasn't looking at the watch at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mrs. Jusufi, that you and your husband couldn't call anyone, since your phone stopped working; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, we couldn't call anyone because we didn't have a phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So nobody was able to come and help you; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Well, there was no way they could come and help us. There was no way they could pass through those bullets. They were shooting from the terrace. All this noise was coming from the terrace, the noise of the bullets. We couldn't go outside at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that when darkness fell outside, that then your neighbours and relatives came, and that then they moved the body of your son inside the house of your daughter in the neighbourhood Durmisina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, at 2.00 in the morning, 1.00 or 2.00. I don't know, I didn't look at the watch. It was dark. I didn't have any light. And please don't ask me any more questions. I am tired. I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a few more, please.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Please don't ask me any more questions, because I will faint now. I can't go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mrs. Jusufi, if you just settle for a moment, there are very few questions left. I think it won't be of any value to you -- I don't think it will be of any value to you to come back tomorrow, which is what we would have to do. You really want to be finished with this. We all appreciate that. So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not coming back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we'll finish tonight, then, yes. Yes, Ms. Residovic. I think you must be near your end.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, let me just ask you: Is it correct that nobody took a picture of your son when in your presence?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: What you're saying doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would just wish at the end to ask you, Mrs. Jusufi: In the questions that I've asked you, you will agree with me that regarding numerous issues, you have given different statements in your previous statements and in the testimony today? Have you observed this?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: As I said, even if I live for another 300 years, I will never forget what happened, and of course I will not change what I've already stated. I'm a 70-year-old woman, 60, 70 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you, Mrs. Jusufi, that you have seen your deceased son for the first time when he was brought into the house of your daughter in the Durmisina neighbourhood, considering that you are testifying under oath, you would certainly agree that that was -- were correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I didn't see him killed there in her house. He was killed in my own house. He wasn't killed in Durmisina house; he was killed at the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you have seen him when he was brought already dead in the house of your daughter?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I saw him in my own house. We took his body to my daughter's house in -- in the early morning hours, 1.00 or 2.00. But when he died, he was in my own house. I don't know why this has been recorded in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were again to tell you, Mrs. Jusufi, that you went to the house of your daughter on Saturday evening, together with your daughter-in-law and your grandchildren --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't go there on Saturday. That's not correct. I didn't go to my daughter's house on Saturday. I was in my own house. What you're saying is a mistake. You're putting things the way you like them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the end, Mrs. Jusufi, in your house in the village of Ljuboten, to that house you have returned only a month later when your son was buried again in the graveyard in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we were afraid to take him to the graveyard. There was no place we could take him to. There was shooting. Even when we returned, the shooting continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusufi, I'm just finishing, but maybe you failed to understand me properly. Is it correct that when you went to your daughter's house in the Durmisina neighbourhood, you and your husband did not return to Ljuboten, to your own house, for a month's time, almost up until the time when your son was transferred to the graveyard in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Three weeks, about a month. I don't know, I forgot, but my husband knows these things better.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Nobody was living in your -- residing in your house during that time?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, whoever could went inside and outside my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mrs. Jusufi, for making the effort to answer my questions. Thank you, Your Honour. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have changed my words. You have mixed things up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we'll see if that's correct. Mr. Apostolski, is there anything you wish to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, although the examination by my colleague, Edina Residovic, was quite exhaustive, I have prepared many questions to ask this witness. I will try not to repeat from what my colleague, Edina Residovic, stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Apostolski, you certainly may ask questions, but I hope they are relevant to what are the real issues in the case. Unfortunately, all counsel so far today have asked questions that go outside the important issues. We have spent a lot of time. We have tired the witness, and we are going to lose time if we move at this pace. So if you please could try and concentrate on the important issues, as far as concerns your client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to be as precise and as concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Jusufi. I am Antonio Apostolski, Defence attorney of Johan Tarculovski. I regret about the loss of your son. I know it must be difficult for you to speak about those moments once again, but you have to have an understanding that I have to ask you several questions in respect to the event. Are you prepared -- so I would start with the questions --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I'm really tired, and I already said what I knew. You can go on speaking, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're being very brave, Mrs. Jusufi, and we're very grateful, but I know that you will find it in you to just deal with a few more questions and then we can, hopefully, allow you to finish and go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't have anything else to add to what I already said, not today or tomorrow. When my husband comes, you can ask him more questions, but this is all I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your evidence is very valuable, and the point is that there are many things about which you have been able to help us that your husband might not be able to. So instead of us just talking, I think we'll ask Mr. Apostolski -- would you please listen to me, Mrs. Jusufi? I know it's hard for you, but the option is this: Either you have to listen and answer questions tonight, or even though you may not like it, you will need to come back and go through more tomorrow. And I think that will be worse for you than if we can finish tonight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I'm not coming back. My husband is waiting outside. He can come and testify, but I want to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's your evidence we need, Mrs. Jusufi. So, Mr. Apostolski, would you just ask your important questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is the statement that you gave today upon the approval of your husband?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: My husband's statement is a separate one. He will come and testify for himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have water in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have water inside your house or is the water in the yard?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: In the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did any of your -- does any member of your family possess a mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Maybe they do. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your son have a mobile phone during the event?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. I forgot. I don't know whether he had or he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have a basement in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, we don't have a basement. We don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have a garage in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, we were in the process of building that garage. We still had not covered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about Friday, August 10, 2001. Was anything unusual happening?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you hearing shootings of any kind? We are talking about two days before the event.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, we could hear shootings. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could the shootings be seen from your yard?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where were you on Friday?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was your husband on Friday, August 10?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: At home, at home. Where can he go in a wheelchair?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was he at home all the time? Was he inside the home or in the yard?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I can't remember that. It was a long time ago. I can't remember what I had for lunch today.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is the statement that you have given today to my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, is based on your memories, on your recollections?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: This is what I know. I remember the day and I will never forget it. Even if I lived 300 years, I will never forget that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that upon your memory or from the tellings of someone else?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, on my own memory. Nobody told me anything. I know, for myself, what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What was your -- where was your son, Rami Jusufi, on August 10, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe he was at the watermelon field, maybe he was in the market selling watermelons. I really don't know. I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When did you go to bed on Friday evening, August 10, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know. I went to sleep in my own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On Saturday, August 11, 2001, could shootings from fire-arms be heard still?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't think -- I don't think they shot on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Who was in your house on Saturday morning?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No one. I didn't have any guests.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you remember where your son was, where your son Rami was on Saturday?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He was in the market to sell watermelon.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When did he return; could you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't remember at what time. I didn't look at the watch. After selling the watermelons, he returned. I don't know the exact hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was that during the day or after dark?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: During the day. They could hardly pass through the check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was your younger son, Salahedin?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was he in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did he stay overnight in his house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Which of my sons?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Salahedin.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He slept in his own house. He had his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you want to confirm that Salahedin was at home on Saturday night?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: He wasn't at my -- at our home. He was in his own house. In his own house he was with his own -- with his own kids.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did anyone come in your house on Saturday evening?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask if we could go on to a closed session, because I will mention a name of a witness that will be heard later on. So in order to -- who might ask for protection by the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop asking me. I want to go. All your questions seem irrelevant to me. I'm not a soldier. They might know what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski wants to go into private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What room did your husband sleep in?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: In the same room with our son.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I, too, slept in the same room. The three of us slept in the same room. We didn't sleep outside in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you all slept in one room?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. The daughter-in-law wasn't there, so we slept in the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When your daughter-in-law is at home, where does she sleep?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: In their room.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which one is their room?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: It was upstairs. You want me to tell you the exact place where they sleep?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I want you to tell me only what is the room that your son sleeps in with his wife?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Why should you know? Is it necessary for you to know that? They have their own room.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: They have their own separate room. Please don't ask me questions which make no sense at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that -- is it correct that your son, together with his wife, are sleeping on the upper floor, up on the -- up the staircase?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, this is where their room is, the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your son usually sleeps on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, he usually sleeps upstairs with his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was his wife on Saturday evening?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: She was afraid and scared from the shots, and she left and went to stay with my daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you usually close the gate of the yard at night? "Lock it." I apologise.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you lock the gate on Saturday night?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Before going to sleep every night, we locked the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Who locks the door at night -- the gate at night?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Whoever can. We don't have a certain person doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is your gate being locked with?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Like everybody else, we use the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like you to answer to me correctly. What exactly do you lock your gate with?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: With a lock, of course. I suppose you do the same. With a key.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Except for the key, is there any other locking mechanism for the gate?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you say that that is a mechanism made of iron with a rod?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the statement of October 3, 2004, 2D1, page 2, paragraph 5, you say that at 5.00, you saw police in front of your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: We saw them going towards the church. We heard them talking from inside the house, so we went inside and heard them talking outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You previously stated, upon the examination of my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, that you have only heard them. Now you are saying that you have seen them as well?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I heard them talking. I didn't see them with my own eyes. I told you, I didn't go outside, I mean out of the gate in the street. We were inside the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me remind you that in the statement given on October 3, 2004, 2D1, page 2, paragraph 8, you say that you have seen cars and trucks on the street. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Don't keep telling me, "You've said this," "You've said that." I don't want to hear that. I'm telling you, we heard them talk. We didn't see them. The mountain was full of tanks, tanks with cannons.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you say where, approximately, those tanks were with the cannons?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: On the mountain. All of us saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you personally see those tanks?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the tanks from the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Although my colleague didn't ask this question, I would like to repeat it because I want to ask -- to accomplish something with it. Who was --

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I am tired, I am tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you again, who was in your house together with you on Sunday morning?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No one was there, only Muzafer. Nobody else. What I know, I know. You are asking me again and again and again who was there, who was there. It doesn't make sense. I'm ready to leave now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have stated that the Kamberi family is your -- are your neighbours? Are you aware of the name "Fatmir Kamberi"?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Of course I know them. They are my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen Fatmir Kamberi during the weekend between August 10 and August 12, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since my colleague, Edina, had quite comprehensive -- asked quite comprehensive questions regarding the clothes he was wearing, I would like to ask you: What was the colour of your son's pyjamas?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: Don't ask me any more, please. His pyjamas were white. He took off the pyjamas and put on some clothes. You want to know what colour his pyjamas were? This is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where were you standing when your son was hit?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: What do you mean, armed? He wasn't armed. In the room, we were in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I did not mention that he was armed. I didn't say he was armed. I just asked you: Where were you standing, precisely, when your son was hit?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I'm telling you, we were in the room. I'm repeating it. In the room. The son left the room, and then he was killed at the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What was the position of your son in relation to the door?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: About to open the door.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Close the door, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was your son turned towards the door with his stomach?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I saw him falling down on the ground -- on the floor. I didn't pay attention to the position he was in at that moment. I just saw him falling down. As soon as I saw him, I fainted. Please don't ask me such questions any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation of the question is not correct. Just a moment. It should be: "Where was your son turned at --"

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I didn't see him, in what position he was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Where was your son facing?"

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you several difficult questions for you, but I have to ask them.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't want to hear any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The time has come when we must finish for the day. It is necessary for the accused to be back --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Jusufi. Mrs. Jusufi --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My husband is waiting outside and is tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We are all tired, but I am sure you are more tired than most of us, and we are very sorry for that. Mr. Apostolski, we must finish at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think you are sorry, since you are keeping me here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is what is involved, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 7.00 now. Will I be able to continue with my questions tomorrow, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not coming here anymore. I'm not going to come here anymore. You are mixing up questions, asking me the same things, asking me the same questions about the same thing, so please don't ask me anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I have maybe three questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be necessary, then, for the evidence to continue tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, I don't want any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... as well, as you know, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not coming tomorrow. My husband is outside. Why did you bring him here?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution could forego the questions on redirect, if that would mean Mrs. Jusufi would finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Apostolski, you were going to move to some different area --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm finished, I'm finished. Don't ask me any more questions. I don't want to hear any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you going to go over the ground that has already been covered by Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would have a few more questions that have not been covered by Mrs. -- by my colleague, Edina Residovic. There are only a few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must adjourn now for the evening. The evidence will continue tomorrow at 2.15, and following this witness will be the evidence of her husband. We want to thank you very much for the help you've tried to give us today, Mrs. Jusufi. We know it's very hard for you, and we adjourn now until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
